question.:question/problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(t,z)=⟨8 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{x^{2}}{64}+\frac{y^{2}}{64}=1.$ What is the second component of $\mathbf{f}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall that the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{64}+\frac{y^{2}}{64}=1$ in the $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨8 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)}⟩,\quad t\in[0,2\pi),
$$

since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x^2}{64}+\frac{y^2}{64}&=\frac{(8 \cos{\left(t \right)})^2}{64}+\frac{(8 \sin{\left(t \right)})^2}{64}\\&=\cos^2 t+\sin^2 t\\&=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\mathbf{f}(t,z)=⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨8 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,8 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,z⟩
$$

where $t\in[0,2\pi)$ and $z\in(-\infty,\infty)$.

Therefore, the second component of $\mathbf{f}$ is $8 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.
